claims.statement: ORNLSlicer declares 28 focused standalone C++ test executables, each linked to the shared ornlslicer_obj production object library and registered under an unprefixed CTest name.
The ORNLSLICER_BUILD_TESTS option defaults to CTest's BUILD_TESTING value and guards test target creation and CTest registration.
Focused tests use executable main functions and shared boolean expectation and numeric-tolerance helpers rather than an external test framework.
The generic development preset uses Clang and Ninja Multi-Config in build/generic-llvm-ninja, so CTest needs the selected configuration such as Debug.

Focused geometry coverage includes mesh repair, fixed and adaptive layer generation, support-gap counts, optimizer ordering and anchors, global layer ordering, and planar, WAAM, and helical path behaviors.
Settings and session regressions cover G-code settings import, version migration, transactional preference import, preference persistence, and recent-project and project-loading behavior.
Parser, writer, and visualization regressions cover common parser inference, Arc Specialties syntax, JuggerBot extrusion behavior, and stable visualization color mappings.
As-printed export tests validate generated bead and centerline geometry, coordinate conventions, filtering, curved geometry, and binary and ASCII STL artifacts.
Adding a tests source file does not automatically register a test because every test executable and add_test entry is declared explicitly in CMake.
File-oriented focused tests use temporary directories for disposable fixtures, reducing dependence on persistent user preferences and output paths.
Qt-dependent focused tests use QCoreApplication rather than a widget application, so they validate core data flow rather than an interactive GUI or OpenGL rendering session.
The new_impact_project_regression test is registered only when a configured local .s2p project path exists and runs the built application through its project-input and output-location arguments.
The optional whole-project regression accepts success only when slicing exits with status zero and creates a nonempty G-code file; it does not compare output with a golden file.
Current push CI runs Nix flake checks on Ubuntu and macOS, builds and smoke-tests the Linux AppImage with --help, and cross-builds Windows portable and installer artifacts.

The current CI workflow does not explicitly invoke CTest, and the Nix package derivation does not define a test check phase, so a green packaging run is not evidence that the focused CTest suite executed.
The suite includes bounded offscreen widget and shader-rendering tests but does not drive full main-window and native-dialog workflows or demonstrate physical controller acceptance.

The added focused lanes cover comparator validation and result semantics, rejection of project-local/session JSON by the global-template loader without rewriting it, and offscreen toolbar visibility plus constrained-width overflow behavior.
The shading regression renders production shaders with OpenGL 4.4 and checks hue and luminance; context or surface unavailability returns 77, which CTest treats as skip.
Standalone layer export and bundled changelog behavior have dedicated focused C++ tests, while release/version rules use a separate Python suite with real Git/CMake/Nix scenarios.
